before_snapshot.comment: FERROCHROME/AOD SUPPLY REVISION, 2026-10-20. This supersedes historical 83%ordinary-steel+17%pure-Cr statements copied in charger comments. The native chromium-production documentation explicitly restricts its 75%aluminothermic/25%electrolytic route to superalloys and says ordinary stainless steels use ferrochrome. Its0.498kgAl/kgCr caused an inappropriate 0.08466kg upstream aluminium purchase per kg of this430reference. Do not replace the alloy by nickel-bearing18/8. Outokumpu describes ferrochrome charging and AOD decarburization; https://www.outokumpu.com/en/expertise/2016/how-stainless-steel-is-made ; https://www.outokumpu.com/investors/-/media/83070B523A6D46CA9F5388A7E9A08AE9.ashx?modified=20170927102955&revision=ae0dbdda-5fea-434a-984a-9cb5dd27746a . Retain17wt%Cr final alloy and the existing 1kg output, all charger quantities, geometry, service and final WEEE. Select an explicit high-carbon68wt%Cr feed,7wt%C,1wt%Si,balanceFe; the Cr assay follows the native reference product. Carbon/silicon are engineering assays, not a certificate for the market. Published Cr-C-Si-Fe measurements https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-98274-8 illustrate their variability; test6-9%C,0.2-1.5%Si and a55%Cr charge-grade alternative. The ordinary-steel precursor is represented as0.1wt%C,0.1wt%Si,balanceFe. Final reference0.04wt%C and0.35wt%Si,Fe remainder; other trace alloy elements including Mn/Ni are unassayed, not proven absent. Use97%netCr retention and100%Fe retention reference; sensitivities include95-99.5%Cr and3%Fe loss. GrossFeCr=0.17/(0.68*0.97)=0.257731958762887kg; Fe-balanced ordinary steel=0.765775881660228kg. Chromium lost after slag reduction is Cr2O3,Fe loss isFeO, excessSi and addedAl becomeSiO2/Al2O3. This is a net reaction ledger, not two purchases of oxidized and subsequently recovered chromium. Choulet,Praxair1999,TableVII,p13 https://device.report/m/af6298efc849d2d62bf2c22f5def38f0bf787435364a6cd75cac7d6d6e91461b.pdf reports AISI304 AOD consumptions:12Nm3Ar/t,9-11Nm3N2/t,50-60kg lime/t,3kg fluorspar/t, 2kgAl/t,8-9kgSi/t,5-9kgbrick/t,96-97%Cr yield. Transfer12,10,55,3,2,8.5,7 and97% respectively as explicit refining analogues; they are NOT measured430plant consumptions. Interpret the source ton as1000kg; test the alternative907.18474kg short-ton normalization. Do not transfer nickel or extra135kg decarburization metallics on top of the balanced feed. A430 BOF/AOD paper https://doi.org/10.1002/srin.202100852 supports the process class, but its different integrated plant is not used to infer this recipe or calibrate its EF result. Keep the existing1kWh+4MJ/kg remelt/finish allowance; its industrial adequacy, rolling/pickling, cooling water and manufacturing infrastructure remain unverified. Gases are purchased as liquid-air products: an explicit conservative delivery proxy including liquefaction; actual onsite gaseous supply may differ. Nm3 is ideal gas at273.15K and101325Pa, R=8.31446261815324J/mol/K. Carbon leaves the AOD asCO; model complete subsequent oxidation toCO2 using ambient air, not a second liquid-oxygen purchase. Purchase only 0.0382295785382025kg bath oxygen (26.7790677252952Nm3/t). Carbon provenance is conservatively fossil in the reference, not established by an actual charge assay. Test CO postcombustion and fossil/nonfossil alternatives explicitly. Neither carbon is burned twice nor energy recovered/credited. N2 is emitted once to generic air. Ambient O2=0.0245186746239282kg and ventedAr=0.0213873762537807kg remain in the mass ledger/documentation only: these uncharacterized flow conventions are unavailable in some older biospheres, so do not insert new unsupported elementary flows. Nominal slag plus conserved lime/fluorspar/spentbasicrefractory=0.0943117313423262kg is sent once to inert-waste disposal, an explicit mineral-containment proxy, not proof of hazard classification or measured recycling. The97%fluorspar stock is conserved at purchased total mass; no invented pure-CaF2 assay, HF emission or recovered-fluoride credit. Cr(VI), HF, entrained dust, slag leaching, actual offgas treatment and auxiliary losses remain missing industrial evidence. Test underground containment as an alternative; do not assert that absence of an exchange proves100%abatement. Slag chemistry, finishing and minor elements remain coverage gaps. Chromium indicator already includes68/55%FeCr, so no method change is required. No new primary/secondary mix or recycling credit. Existing supplemental workbook only; no native/runtime/YAML edits.

CLIC_snapshot.comment: Qualified grade-430 charger-alloy engineering reference, not a measured mill inventory. Nominal 17% Cr, 0.04% C, 0.35% Si and Fe remainder; 97% Cr and 100% Fe retention. The chromium-yield benchmark covers combined EAF/AOD AISI304, not grade430 AOD alone. Ferrochrome/steel assays, metric-ton normalization, liquid-gas supply, full fossil-CO oxidation, N2/Ar release and inert-residue disposal are the separately approved modelling proxies. Ambient postcombustion oxygen is documented, not bought again. 1 kWh electricity and 4 MJ heat per kg cover a broad remelt/finish allowance. Casting, rolling, cutting, bending and coating are not individually quantified; Cr(VI), HF, dust and leaching are coverage gaps, not proven zero. No nickel assay, measured abatement, legal waste classification, recovery credit or complete fabrication is claimed. Authority: R85-R95, with nominal inputs and outlet quantities retained.
